stories.title: CMBS Loan Backed by Vornado, Related’s 85 10th Avenue Sent to Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: A $396 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan secured by 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-square-foot office property in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent maturity default, according to an alert from Morningstar Credit. 85 10th Avenue is owned jointly by Vornado Realty Trust and the Related Companies. Related purchased the property in 2007 from Somerset Partners for $430 million and brought Vornado in as a 50/50 partner. The $396 million loan makes up DBWF 2016-85T and is part of larger conduits CD 2017-CD3 and BACM 2017-BNK3. It is expected to default ahead of its December 2026 maturity date, according to Morningstar. The building’s largest tenant, Google, currently takes up 47 percent of its space, as the firm has gradually expanded since signing a 180,000-square-foot lease in 2014. But cash flow from rents has declined lately, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. Morningstar Credit reports that 85 10th Avenue’s cash flow fell 28 percent below underwriting in 2025, and that biometric screening company CLEAR, which signed a 120,000-square-foot lease for a new headquarters in 2021, is currently in a rent abatement period. Vornado reported that the building’s occupancy stood at 89 percent in its most recent second-quarter earnings supplemental. The 11-story 85 10th Avenue first opened in 1913 as a Nabisco factory and was redeveloped for commercial office use in the late 1990s. Vornado and Related invested into renovating the lobby in 2023. Vornado and Related did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vornado/Related's 85 10th Avenue ($396M CMBS loan) sent to special servicing; imminent default ahead of Dec 2026 maturity.
Google occupies 47% (180K SF) of 633K SF Chelsea office tower; post-COVID cash flow declined materially.
Manhattan office distress signals weak demand recovery; refinance window closing for overleveraged assets.
stories.summary: A $396 million CMBS loan backing the Vornado/Related-owned 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-square-foot office tower in Chelsea, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent default ahead of its December 2026 maturity. Google, the building's largest tenant, occupies 47% of the space but cash flow from rents has declined since the COVID-19 pandemic. The loan default reflects sustained office market weakness and the closing window for refinance opportunities in Manhattan.
stories.impact: Manhattan office distress at trophy assets signals that even marquee tenants (Google) cannot sustain pre-pandemic rent levels or occupancy economics. This underscores structural headwinds to office conversion feasibility and validates multifamily demand fundamentals in Manhattan—residential will absorb displaced office workers and households seeking housing security over speculative workplace leases.

stories.title: Newgard Group Buys West Palm Dev Site to Build Car-Centric Private Club
stories.excerpt: Harvey Hernandez’s Newgard Group bought a development site in West Palm Beach, Fla., to build an upscale parking garage with a private members club component. The Miami-based developer paid $10.5 million for a 2.6-acre parcel at 2500 North Florida Mango Road, just north of Palm Beach International Airport, property records show. Called Palm Beach Auto Haus, the upcoming two-story development will be a private members club with space to park 20 cars and amenities that include padel courts, coworking lounges, a cafe and a gym. The project marks somewhat of a departure for a new-to-market developer in West Palm Beach, most of whom have launched luxury condo developments near the city’s waterfront. “For years I searched for a place that reflected the way passionate automobile enthusiasts truly enjoy their collections,” Hernandez, founder and CEO of Newgard Group, said in a statement. “We envisioned something far beyond traditional car storage — a destination centered around ownership, design, community and unforgettable experiences.” Newgard Group nabbed a $6.3 million acquisition loan from Belmont Bank & Trust. The seller, a Thousand Oaks, Calif.-based entity tied to Jonathan and Justin Bergman, had purchased the asset, which holds a 29,790-square-foot commercial building, for $3.5 million in 2021. The Bergmans could not be reached for comment. In Miami’s Brickell district, Newgard Group is building a waterfront, luxury condo complex alongside Two Roads Development, after securing a $513 million debt package last year. Earlier this month, it sold off a piece of land for $50 million to another development team. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Newgard Group ($10.5M) acquires 2.6-acre West Palm Beach site for auto club + parking, not residential.
Market shift: developer pursues amenity-driven non-residential use (coworking, padel, café, gym) near airport.
West Palm Beach land conversion away from multifamily indicates rising land costs or developer view of higher-margin mixed uses.
stories.summary: Newgard Group paid $10.5 million for a 2.6-acre parcel in West Palm Beach near Palm Beach International Airport to develop Palm Beach Auto Haus, a two-story private members' club with 20 parking spaces and amenities including padel courts, coworking lounges, a café, and a gym. The project represents a departure from typical waterfront luxury condo development in West Palm Beach.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily unless interpreted as signal that West Palm land values have risen sufficiently to justify non-residential uses or that developer perceives higher risk/lower returns in residential. The coworking and amenity mix suggests target demographic (affluent auto enthusiasts) prefers experiential lifestyle components—a trend multifamily should monitor for mixed-use and resident experience design.

stories.title: After 30-Year Hold, Monarch Offloads Golden Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Monarch Investment & Management Group sold Fox Hill Apartments, a 153-unit garden-style community in Golden, Colorado for $32 million. Monarch Investment & Management Group owned Fox Hill for nearly 30 years. Sierra Parkway Communities was the buyer. JLL represented Monarch in the sale of the property. JLL Capital Market’s Sales and Advisory team was led by Jordan Robbins, Wick Kirby, Alex Possick and Seth Gallman. JLL asserts that the 1972-built property at 17611 W. 16th Ave. presents a value-add opportunity, with the ability to renovate 100% of its unit interiors to a standardized scope while enhancing outdoor amenity spaces. The average in-place rent of $1,645 sits significantly below the area’s $908,000 median home price, creating a 3.30-times premium to own versus rent within a one-mile radius. Current rent levels represent just 15% of average household incomes exceeding $128,000 in the immediate area. The property maintains 95% occupancy and has averaged 96% occupancy since 2021. bullets: Monarch sells Fox Hill Apartments (153 units, Golden, CO) for $32M after 30-year hold to Sierra Parkway Communities.
In-place rent $1,645 significantly below area: 3.3x premium to own; rents only 15% of $128K+ household incomes.
95% occupancy, 100% unit renovation upside; value-add arbitrage signals strong Golden rental demand and affordability gap.
stories.summary: Monarch Investment & Management Group sold Fox Hill Apartments, a 153-unit garden-style community in Golden, Colorado, to Sierra Parkway Communities for $32 million after nearly 30 years of ownership. The 1972-built property has in-place rents of $1,645, significantly below the $908,000 median home price in the area, creating a 3.3x ownership premium and rents representing only 15% of average household incomes exceeding $128,000. The property maintains 95% occupancy with strong leasing history.
stories.impact: Golden, CO multifamily demonstrates resilient demand and substantial value-add opportunity in a supply-constrained mountain market. The wide rent-to-home-price gap and low rent-to-income ratio signal that rents can support higher pricing post-renovation and positioning; acquisition and asset-management flexibility drives returns in markets with constrained new supply and affluent, stable employment bases (tech, professional services).

stories.title: Health Care Tech Company SuperDial Takes 5K SF at GFP’s 322 Eighth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Health care technology company SuperDial has inked a full-floor lease at GFP Real Estate’s 322 Eighth Avenue, according to a Wednesday announcement by the landlord. SuperDial’s 5,200-square-foot lease spans the entire 20th floor of the Chelsea office tower on the northeast corner of Eighth Avenue and West 26th Street. It is the largest deal among nearly 10,000 square feet of recent leasing activity there. Rent prices within the 20-story building were not disclosed, but asking rents for Midtown South office space averaged $86.38 per square foot in July, according to CBRE data. Allen Gurevich represented GFP in-house in the recent deals, while CBRE’s Harry Singer negotiated on behalf of SuperDial. The San Francisco-based company, which uses artificial intelligence to automate phone calls between health care teams and insurers, currently lists a New York office at RFR and Raycliff Capital’s 875 Washington Street. It is unclear whether the recent deal at 322 Eighth Avenue marks a relocation or expansion for the tech company. GFP’s 322 Eighth Avenue has also secured a seven-year renewal from nonprofit Institute for Human Identity. The psychotherapy and training center, which provides affirmative psychotherapy to the LGBTQ community, maintains a 2,652-square-foot office on the building’s eighth floor. GFP will renovate the institute’s existing space as part of the renewal. GRP’s Gurevich represented the nonprofit in the direct transaction, as well as its newest neighbor, mental health practice Chelsea Therapy Space. The practice signed a five-year lease for a newly customized 2,100-square-foot office on a portion of the eighth floor. Chelsea Therapy Space encompasses providers Chelsea Therapeutic Space, Equity Therapy Marriage and Family Therapy, Kingfisher Marriage and Family Therapy, according to the landlord. bullets: SuperDial (AI healthcare tech) leases full 5.2K SF floor (20th) at GFP's 322 Eighth Avenue, Chelsea; largest of ~10K SF recent activity.
Midtown South office asking rents average $86.38/SF; unclear if relocation or expansion from existing RFR/Raycliff space.
Tech tenant leasing activity in office suggests selective corporate real estate commitment amid uncertain remote work hybrid policies.
stories.summary: AI-powered healthcare technology company SuperDial signed a full-floor lease for 5,200 square feet on the 20th floor of GFP Real Estate's 322 Eighth Avenue in Chelsea, marking the largest deal among approximately 10,000 square feet of recent leasing activity. Midtown South office asking rents averaged $86.38 per square foot. SuperDial currently has an office at RFR and Raycliff Capital's 875 Washington Street, and it is unclear whether this represents a relocation or expansion.
stories.impact: Tech tenant absorption in Midtown South office remains selective and floor-by-floor rather than portfolio-scale, indicating continued caution on office occupancy commitments. This selective leasing supports multifamily demand narrative—tech workers and their households prioritize residential flexibility and lifestyle proximity over traditional office footprints, sustaining renter-in-place preferences in mixed-use neighborhoods like Chelsea and Hudson Square.

stories.title: BH Adds Nearly 300K-SF Asset to Plano Office Portfolio
stories.excerpt: BH Properties completed the acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-square-foot, seven-building business park in Plano, Texas. The acquisition follows the firm’s February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing BH’s ownership within the Legacy Business Park to more than 675,000 square feet across fourteen buildings. BH acquired the property from KBS. KBS was represented by Newmark’s Dallas team of Gary Carr, Chris Murphy, Robert Hill, and Austin Sheahan, while BH was represented by Scott Henry. Currently, approximately 70% leased, Tollway North consists of seven single-story office buildings totaling nearly 300,000 square feet and provides tangible value-add opportunities. Stream Realty’s Chase Lopez, James Mantzuranis, and Sam Bass in Dallas will be representing BH on leasing. The area is home to numerous Fortune 500 and global companies, with AT&T’s planned global headquarters expected to bring thousands of its employees to the immediate area beginning in 2028. Connect Texas Multifamily in Dallas on August 13 brings together the owners, developers, brokers, investors, and lenders shaping the future of Texas multifamily for a day of market intelligence, networking, and actionable insights. Join 300+ decision-makers and be part of the conversations driving the Texas multifamily market. Register today: www.ConnectTXMF2026.com. bullets: BH Properties acquires Tollway North Office Park (297.6K SF, 7 buildings) in Plano, TX; ~70% leased, value-add.
Follows Feb 2025 purchase of adjacent R&D at Legacy; BH now owns 675K+ SF across 14 buildings in Legacy Business Park.
AT&T global headquarters expected to drive thousands of employees to area beginning 2028; portfolio positioned for tenant backfill.
stories.summary: BH Properties completed the acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-square-foot, seven-building business park in Plano, Texas, currently approximately 70% leased. This follows BH's February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing BH's ownership within the Legacy Business Park to more than 675,000 square feet across fourteen buildings. The area is home to numerous Fortune 500 and global companies, with AT&T's planned global headquarters expected to bring thousands of employees beginning in 2028.
stories.impact: AT&T HQ relocation to Plano (2028 launch) signals major employment influx and population in-migration to Dallas market; multifamily developers should fast-track acquisitions and entitlements in Plano, North Dallas, and Legacy Park corridors to capture rent growth from 2027–2030 as AT&T talent and service vendors relocate. Office value-add portfolios upstream of residential can de-risk land assembly and pre-lease conversations.

stories.title: Teeple Adding 312-Unit Student Housing Project to Texas A&M Offering
stories.excerpt: Teeple Partners started construction on its newest apartment development, Oaks Reserve. The 312-unit community will be situated along the Innovation Corridor in the Bryan-College Station market, midway between Texas A&M University’s RELLIS Research Campus and the Texas A&M Health Science Center. Oaks Reserve is the second phase of a planned three-phase multifamily development encompassing more than 53 acres and totaling approximately 1,000 apartment homes. The first phase, Brazos Oaks (shown), consists of 315 units and was completed in June 2026. The community has experienced strong demand and is now over 90% leased. Apartment homes will have private yards with amenities that include a swimming pool, a state-of-the-art fitness facility, a conference room, a resident lounge, private workspaces and focus rooms, a package locker system, two pickleball courts and separate dog parks for small and large dogs. The community was designed by HLR Architects. Construction is being managed by Interwest Construction. Construction and permanent financing are being provided by Mason Joseph Company. The post Teeple Adding 312-Unit Student Housing Project to Texas A&M Offering appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Teeple Partners begins construction on Oaks Reserve (312 units) in Bryan-College Station, TX; Phase 2 of 1,000-unit, 53-acre project.
Phase 1 (Brazos Oaks, 315 units, completed June 2026) now 90%+ leased, demonstrating strong student/workforce demand near Texas A&M.
Location: Innovation Corridor between RELLIS Research Campus and Texas A&M Health Science Center; long-term institutional anchor.
stories.summary: Teeple Partners has begun construction on Oaks Reserve, a 312-unit student housing community in Bryan-College Station, Texas, positioned along the Innovation Corridor midway between Texas A&M University's RELLIS Research Campus and the Texas A&M Health Science Center. The project is the second phase of a planned three-phase development encompassing more than 53 acres and approximately 1,000 apartment homes. Phase 1 (Brazos Oaks, 315 units) was completed in June 2026 and is now over 90% leased.
stories.impact: Texas A&M expansion (RELLIS, Health Science Center) and Innovation Corridor job creation are driving sustained multifamily demand in Bryan-College Station. Phase 1's 90%+ occupancy post-delivery validates institutional tenant demand and positioning; Phase 2 and 3 are de-risked by proof-of-concept, enabling faster execution and financing. Developers should replicate institutional-proximity model in other university and R&D-heavy Texas markets.

stories.title: Stonepeak Picks Up 860K-SF Rail-Served DFW Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Stonepeak acquired an 860,100-square-foot rail-served logistics asset in Fort Worth, Texas. The asset is located in the Alliance submarket of Dallas-Fort Worth, which is anchored by two Class I rail lines, the BNSF Alliance intermodal terminal, and the Fort Worth Alliance cargo airport, with direct access to the I-35 “NAFTA highway” linking Mexico to Canada. The Alliance submarket’s transport infrastructure is supported by DFW’s population of 9 million residents, which is expected to grow by 3x the national average through 2031. Stonepeak’s real estate team invests in assets that exhibit infrastructure characteristics. The team invests in supply chain, residential, healthcare and technology real estate. The team targets opportunities with high barriers to entry, inflation protection, and are mission-critical to the businesses and communities they serve. Newmark served as financial advisor to Stonepeak. The post Stonepeak Picks Up 860K-SF Rail-Served DFW Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stonepeak acquires 860.1K SF rail-served warehouse in Fort Worth Alliance submarket (DFW).
DFW population 9M, expected to grow 3x national average through 2031; Alliance anchored by BNSF, intermodal, cargo airport.
Infrastructure-critical logistics asset aligns with Stonepeak's inflation-hedge, high-barrier-entry real estate strategy.
stories.summary: Stonepeak acquired an 860,100-square-foot rail-served logistics asset in Fort Worth's Alliance submarket, anchored by two Class I rail lines, the BNSF Alliance intermodal terminal, Fort Worth Alliance cargo airport, and direct I-35 access. DFW's population of 9 million is expected to grow at 3x the national average through 2031. Stonepeak's real estate team targets assets with high barriers to entry, inflation protection, and mission-critical infrastructure.
stories.impact: DFW population growth (3x national average through 2031) will drive sustained logistics demand and downstream residential in-migration. Multifamily developers should prioritize acquisitions along I-35, north Dallas, and Fort Worth suburban corridors adjacent to Alliance and other logistics hubs; supply chain and logistics worker influx will sustain rent growth and absorption in secondary markets.

stories.title: As Prelude to Texas Multifamily 2026, a Q & A with Nick Jans of Red Oak Capital Holdings

bullets: Red Oak Capital lender panel at Texas Multifamily 2026 (Aug 13, Dallas) previews financing environment reset.
Borrowers now expect sustained higher rates (no near-term dramatic decline); refinance-focused deals dominate; tighter underwriting standards.
Sponsors pursuing perm, bridge, CMBS, agency financing; cash-neutral refinance execution and non-recourse structures preferred.
stories.summary: Nick Jans of Red Oak Capital Holdings, speaking ahead of the Texas Multifamily 2026 conference, indicates that borrower expectations and financing terms have shifted materially. Borrowers now assume sustained elevated interest rates without near-term dramatic decline, and sponsors are focused on cash-neutral refinance execution with non-recourse structures across perm, bridge, CMBS, and agency channels. Underwriting standards have tightened and return thresholds reset.
stories.impact: Financing environment reset means development feasibility thresholds have risen; basis and cost inflation must be offset by higher rents or lower leverage. Developers with low-cost land, entitled projects, and access to patient capital have competitive advantage. Value-add and development projects need 7%–8%+ unlevered returns to attract capital; ground-up starts require dense, high-rent scenarios (urban, institutional, mixed-use) to justify construction risk.

stories.title: Richman Group Secures $225M Loan to Refinance Three South Florida Multifamily Assets
stories.excerpt: The Richman Group, an $18.5 billion asset management firm, has secured $225 million in permanent financing to refinance three stabilized luxury multifamily properties in South Florida that total 942 units. New York Life Investment Management provided $107 million to refinance the Marc Apartments, a 396-unit multifamily property in Palm Beach Gardens. The asset is located at 3955 Design Center Drive and opened in December 2024. New York Life Investment Management also provided $72.5 million to refinance Everly Apartments, a 320-unit community in Naples, Fla. The asset is located at 3250 Magnolia Pond Circle and opened in early 2024. Finally, Reinsurance Group of America provided $45.5 million to refinance Vista Sur Apartments, an eight-story, 226-unit multifamily building in the South Miami neighborhood of Naranja. That asset is located at 27077 South Dixie Highway and opened in 2024. Each of the three loans carries a 10-year term with a five-year interest-only period at interest rates that range from 5.8 percent to 6.1 percent. No brokers were listed on the transactions. Richard Richman, founder of the Richman Group, noted in a statement that his firm closed the $225 million in financings in just four months, in an environment where capital remains constrained and underwriting standards have risen amid industry-wide refinancing challenges. “These closings reflect the strength and stability of our assets, our team’s ability to execute complex transactions, and our successful transition of all three communities into long-term stabilized operations,” he said. Richman founded his eponymous firm in 1986 and has since accumulated a portfolio of more than 2,070 properties, 166,500 units, and $28 billion in total deal volume. The firm has 12 national offices. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Richman Group ($18.5B AUM) secures $225M permanent financing for 3 South Florida luxury multifamily assets (942 units, 2024 deliveries).
New York Life ($107M Marc, $72.5M Everly), RGA ($45.5M Vista Sur); 10-year terms, 5-year IO, rates 5.8%+.
Three newly stabilized properties (Dec 2024–early 2024 opens) already refinancing; strong South Florida luxury rent growth supports permanent financing.
stories.summary: Richman Group secured $225 million in permanent financing to refinance three stabilized luxury multifamily properties totaling 942 units across South Florida: Marc Apartments (396 units, Palm Beach Gardens, opened Dec 2024, $107M); Everly Apartments (320 units, Naples, opened early 2024, $72.5M); and Vista Sur Apartments (226 units, Naranja/South Miami, opened 2024, $45.5M). New York Life provided $179.5M; Reinsurance Group of America provided $45.5M. All loans carry 10-year terms with five-year interest-only periods at rates of 5.8% or higher.
stories.impact: South Florida luxury multifamily is achieving rate stability and permanent-debt viability within 12–18 months of opening; this signals strong rent growth, operational performance, and institutional investor appetite (insurance, pension) for high-quality residential assets in supply-constrained luxury markets. Developers with entitled pipeline in Miami, Broward, Naples should accelerate starts; permanent financing availability validates feasibility even at current construction costs and elevated debt service.

Gov. Hochul highlights $25M R&D investment over 5 years; tech tenant recruitment continues despite office headwinds.

Multifamily developers should monitor Hudson Square, SoHo, and Nolita for residential demand influx from tech worker cohort; mixed-use development (office-to-residential conversion, residential adjacent to tech corridors) de-risks residential absorption in gateway markets.
